Quick write-up of how Q3 went for Ironbark Brewing's trade sales, ahead of
Thursday's board meeting. Figures are from the ERP as of 6 October.

Overall trade revenue was $1.24m, up 9% on Q3 last year but about 4% short of
the plan we set in January. Volume was 4,310 hectolitres. The gap to plan is
almost entirely in the on-premise channel: pubs and restaurants ordered less
keg beer in July during the heatwave than we expected, mostly because two of
our biggest venue groups switched their summer guest taps to a competitor's
lager.

Off-premise did better than expected. The 4-pack can range is now in 212
independent bottle shops (up from 168), and the new hazy pale has been our
fastest-moving SKU in that channel since launch, averaging 1.6 cases per
store per week.

Regionally, the coast held steady, the city grew 14%, and the northern
territory fell 11% after we lost the distributor there in August. Average
selling price per litre rose 3% thanks to the price increase in June, and we
haven't seen evidence that it cost us accounts.

My read: we don't have a demand problem, we have a coverage problem in
on-premise and the north. I'd recommend we hire a second on-premise rep for
the city and run a guest-tap program for venue groups before next summer,
rather than discounting.

Happy to walk through the account-level data on Thursday.

- Marcus Hale, Head of Trade Sales
